open_points.subject: M07 PublicationMark.marked_at
open_points.question: Which time authority supplies the instant written to `marked_at`?
options: a timestamp obtained from the state filesystem
open_points.default_guess: Use an injected system wall clock.

open_points.subject: M07 PublicationMark.marked_at
open_points.text: The calling flow reports the `photo_id` right after `photo.publish` answers, and the deliverer creates the mark.
open_points.question: Which event does `marked_at` denote: receipt of the request, acquisition of the project lock, completion of validation, or creation of the durable mark record?
options: the instant immediately before the mark record is committed
open_points.default_guess: Read the clock once after validation while holding the project lock, immediately before creating the mark record.

witness.initial: A placement exists without a mark, and another call holds the project lock for ten minutes.
events: The calling flow submits the mark request.
The request waits for the project lock.
The deliverer eventually writes the mark record.
outcomes: `marked_at` is the time at which the mark is created under the lock.
witness.observer: A reader of the stored PublicationMark sees timestamps ten minutes apart.

open_points.subject: M07 PublicationMark.marked_at
open_points.question: Must `marked_at` be naive UTC, offset-aware UTC, local time, or another representation?
options: local time using the run setting
open_points.default_guess: Store UTC without an offset, matching the explicitly defined representation used for photo instants.

witness.initial: The service runs in a time zone whose offset is not UTC.
events: The calling flow records a publication mark.
The mark record is serialized and later read.
outcomes: The record contains a naive UTC datetime.
The record contains an offset-aware or local datetime representing the same instant.
witness.observer: The record reader sees a different representation and may compare or serialize it differently.

open_points.subject: mark operation time readings
open_points.text: The first mark stands when it is sent again, and its `marked_at` does not change
open_points.question: How many readings of the time source does a mark operation take, and do replayed or refused mark calls read it at all?
options: one reading only when a fresh mark will be written, and zero for replay or refusal
one reading for every mark request
multiple readings during a fresh mark, with the last one stored
open_points.default_guess: Take exactly one reading for a fresh mark after all refusal and replay checks; take none for a replay or refusal.

witness.initial: A controllable clock returns a different instant on every read; a placement exists without a mark.
events: The caller submits a successful mark request.
The implementation validates and writes the mark.
outcomes: The operation reads the clock once and stores that instant.
The operation reads the clock more than once and stores a later instant.
witness.observer: The caller inspecting the persisted mark sees which clock value was selected.

open_points.subject: A3 INV-06 Required tests
open_points.text: INV-06: a second placement returns the first publication and leaves every stored image and placement record unchanged, with one placement record in place (`test_a_repeated_placement_writes_no_durable_state`).
open_points.question: What must the INV-06 test show about the existing mark record and all other durable writes, given that rule 2 says a replay creates or changes no mark and the invariant says it writes nothing?
options: assert that the mark record is byte-for-byte unchanged and that no durable address is written
check only stored images and placement records as the current item states
open_points.default_guess: Require the test to prove that the existing mark is unchanged and that the replay performs no durable write.

witness.initial: A project already has a placement, stored image and publication mark for the requested content.
events: The caller repeats delivery of that content.
One implementation returns the existing result without writing.
Another implementation rewrites the mark with equivalent data while leaving every stored image and placement record unchanged.
outcomes: No durable state is written, satisfying rule 2 and INV-06.
The stated Required tests assertions still pass, although the mark was written contrary to rule 2 and INV-06.
witness.observer: A filesystem write trace or observer of the mark record's filesystem metadata sees the difference.

open_points.subject: A3 replacement status and INV-07
open_points.text: INV-07: a replaced file is reported as a new photo with the READY member of = models.ScanStatus while the earlier image and mark stay (`test_a_replaced_file_is_a_new_photo_and_the_first_delivery_stays`), and a removed file keeps its delivery (`test_removing_a_file_keeps_its_delivery`).
open_points.question: When a file is replaced by content that already has a placement in the same project, must the scan report READY as this passage says, or PLACED or PUBLISHED under A1 orders 7 and 8 and A3's content identity?
options: PLACED when the replacement content already has a placement and no mark
PUBLISHED when the replacement content already has a placement and mark
READY only when the replacement content has no existing placement
open_points.default_guess: Interpret the Required tests statement as applying only to previously unplaced replacement content; otherwise report PLACED or PUBLISHED according to A1.

witness.initial: A project contains `a.jpg` with content X and `b.jpg` with content Y; Y already has a placement and publication mark.
events: Syncthing replaces `a.jpg` with bytes identical to content Y.
outcomes: A1 orders 7 and 8 and content-based placement identity make `a.jpg` PUBLISHED.
The INV-07 Required tests statement makes the replaced `a.jpg` a new READY photo.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees a different scan status and either offers or suppresses another delivery.
